ops.title: store: three incompatible schema epochs in four days, no migration path, fail-closed with no recovery tooling
ops.description:
Upgrading cc-pool across a store schema change bricks the daemon permanently, with no migration, no export/import, and no diagnostic beyond a bare hex-pair mismatch. Three mutually incompatible schema epochs shipped in four days. Observed in the field on yasyf-home; both machines' daemons have been dead since their upgrades crossed an epoch boundary.

## Symptom

`cc-pool doctor` and `cc-pool sync status` fail immediately:

    store schema mismatch: schema fingerprint 01af1e6d..., want 0efa0acc...

The on-disk value never changes; only the `want` moves with each upgrade.

## Epoch table (fingerprints reproduced from source, validated against both reported values)

| Fingerprint | Releases | Tag date |
|---|---|---|
| `01af1e6db013...` | v0.60.0 - v0.61.7 | 2026-07-21 |
| `fbde893a0ba8...` | v0.62.0 - v0.63.3 | 2026-07-23 |
| `0efa0accdfe8...` | v0.64.0 - v0.64.8 | 2026-07-24/25 |

Replaying each historical `schema` const through sqlite3 and hashing it reproduces HEAD as `0efa0acc...` and v0.63.2 as `fbde893a...`, both exactly matching the values those binaries report. The on-disk `01af1e6d` is therefore a legitimately released schema (introduced at c2147e4, 2026-07-20), not a corrupt or half-migrated artifact - the store is complete and internally consistent, its epoch simply got abandoned by later releases.

## Mechanism

- `schemaHash` (internal/store/store.go:583-604) is SHA-256 over every `sqlite_schema` row (`type`, `name`, `tbl_name`, `sql`, NUL-terminated, `ORDER BY type,name`). It hashes the *literal DDL text*, so any column, CHECK, or whitespace change moves the fingerprint.
- `exactSchemaHash` (store.go:567-581) derives `want` by executing the embedded `const schema` (store.go:32-390) into an in-memory DB; `verifySchema` (store.go:545-565) demands exact equality and returns `ErrSchemaMismatch` (store.go:396).
- This runs on **every open**, not just doctor. `initializeOrVerifySchema` (store.go:523-543) creates a schema only when the DB has zero objects; any existing DB goes straight to exact-equality verification. Reached by `pool.OpenDaemon` (manager.go:145, daemon startup at daemon/server.go:358) and `pool.OpenLocal` (manager.go:177), which every CLI command hits through `withManager` (cli/root.go:104).
- **There is no migration code anywhere.** `grep -i migrat` across every `.go` file in the repo returns zero matches. Commit 04ce289 (2026-07-14) is literally "refactor: remove back-compat, migration, and legacy-version cruft". No env-var escape hatch (zero `os.Getenv` in internal/store/, paths.go, cmd/), no build tags in internal/store/, and no migrate/store subcommand.
- The design intent is stated in CHANGELOG.md:139-142: "Runtime state and every cc-pool-owned protocol start at one fresh epoch: `pool-v1.db` ... Exact equality is required before mutation; old databases and clients fail closed." Fail-closed was chosen deliberately; shipping it without recovery tooling was not.

## Field impact

- Both machines' daemons are dead from the moment their upgrade crossed an epoch. On yasyf-home the daemon last wrote `pool-v1.db` on Jul 22 04:42 and never restarted; no launchd job remains.
- The failure is silent and undiagnosable in the field: two hex prefixes, no mention of versions, epochs, or what to do.
- Every store-touching command refuses - `ccp init` (cli/init.go:20), `doctor` (cli/doctor.go:21), `service install` (cli/service.go:250,261), `sync enable/disable/status/converge` (cli/sync.go:90,106,122,153) - because `withManager` opens the store before any command body runs. **Nothing overwrites a mismatched store, so there is no data-loss risk from running them**, but there is also no way forward.
- **Accounts are not recoverable via `ccp login` alone.** `ccp add` mints a new random 128-bit `instance_id` (store.go:645-646, reserve.go:34) -> new config dir `~/.cc-pool/config/<instanceID>` -> new derived Keychain service `baseService-<first8hex(sha256(configDir))>` (execution_config.go:28-33, creds/keychain.go:81-86). Credential discovery is scoped to the account's own derived service (credential_identity.go:55), so it cannot find items stored under the old names. Every account needs a fresh `claude auth login`, and the old Keychain items become orphaned garbage.

Not lost: no OAuth token is stored in the DB. Every credential column is a 32-byte digest or a Keychain locator; secrets live in the macOS Keychain (see 538590b, "hard cut credentials to Keychain ownership"). Lost on recreate: the `accounts` roster (id, instance_id, generation, config_dir, keychain_service/account, label, account_uuid), `usage_samples` + `refresh_log`, `sticky` cwd pins, `sessions`, `auth_health`, plus by-design-ephemeral journals/receipts.

Note also `~/.cc-pool/pool.db` (the pre-Jul-20 name, renamed by daae973): nothing in current code reads it. `git log -S'"pool.db"'` returns only the initial commit and that rename. It is abandoned legacy, safe to archive.

## Recovery recipe (current workaround, no downgrade required)

The roster is plain SQLite and the schema is known, so no cc-pool binary is needed:

1. Dump the roster read-only:

       sqlite3 -readonly ~/.cc-pool/pool-v1.db \
         "SELECT id,instance_id,label,account_uuid,config_dir,keychain_service,keychain_account
          FROM accounts WHERE deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY id;"

2. Archive `pool-v1.db` (and `pool.db`) out of `~/.cc-pool/`.
3. Let the current binary create a fresh store.
4. Re-add each account with `ccp add` + `claude auth login`, restoring labels from the dump.
5. Clean up the orphaned Keychain items listed under the old `keychain_service` values.

(Alternative for reading the store with a working binary: v0.61.7 is the last release whose schema is `01af1e6d`. That is a read/recovery step only - re-upgrading hits the identical wall.)

## The absence of records is part of the bug

A sweep of this repo's cc-notes (73 notes, 26 docs) for "store schema", "pool-v1", "cutover", "fingerprint", and "schema mismatch" found **no record of the store cutover, no migration intent, and no runbook** - every hit was File Provider / fusekit incident material. Three schema epochs shipped in four days and none of them were recorded, which is why the field failure took a full source investigation to identify.

ops.text: A supported migration or export/import path exists across store schema changes (automatic on daemon start, or an explicit subcommand).
Upgrading across a schema epoch no longer silently kills the daemon: the failure names the on-disk epoch, the binary's expected epoch, and the recovery step, instead of a bare hex-pair mismatch.
If hard-cut epochs are kept deliberately, the policy is documented (CHANGELOG + docs) together with the recovery procedure, and releases that change the schema say so.
